name: Medicare Shared Savings Program
description: CMS flagship ACO program where provider groups coordinate care for Medicare FFS beneficiaries and share savings relative to a benchmark. BASIC and ENHANCED tracks offer varying levels of shared savings and downside risk.

name: Pioneer ACO Model
description: CMMI's first ACO model designed for health systems already experienced in coordinated care. Offered higher shared savings rates and greater downside risk than MSSP. Most participants transitioned to MSSP after model ended.

name: Next Generation ACO Model
description: CMMI model testing higher levels of risk and reward for ACOs experienced with population-based payments. Included prospective attribution, benchmark discounts, and benefit enhancements for beneficiaries.

name: ACO REACH Model
description: Successor to the Global and Professional Direct Contracting Model. ACOs accept prospective attribution and financial accountability (Professional or Global risk) for Medicare FFS beneficiaries, with mandatory Health Equity Plans.

name: Comprehensive Primary Care Plus
description: CMMI multi-payer primary care model offering care management fees and performance-based incentives to primary care practices. Tested in 14 regions with over 2,900 participating practices and 40 payer partners.

name: Primary Care First
description: CMMI model offering a flat primary care visit fee, population-based payment, and performance-based adjustments for primary care practices ready to accept accountability for total cost of care.

name: Making Care Primary
description: Ten-year CMMI primary care model in 8 states with a graduated pathway toward prospective total cost of care accountability. Focuses on care management, behavioral health integration, and specialist partnerships.

name: BPCI Advanced
description: Episode-based payment model for 90-day clinical episodes triggered by inpatient hospitalization. Participants — hospitals or physician group practices — are accountable for quality and cost across 32 clinical episode types. Ran eight model years and concluded December 31, 2025.

name: Comprehensive Care for Joint Replacement
description: Mandatory-then-voluntary episode payment model for hip and knee replacement surgeries. Hospitals bear upside and downside risk for the 90-day post-discharge episode. Initially mandatory in selected markets. Concluded December 31, 2024 after its final performance year.

name: Oncology Care Model
description: Six-year CMMI model for oncology practices providing chemotherapy. Practices received monthly enhanced oncology services payments and could earn performance-based incentives. Predecessor to the Enhancing Oncology Model.

name: Enhancing Oncology Model
description: Successor to OCM. Oncology practices assume downside risk for 6-month chemotherapy episodes across 7 cancer types. Incorporates health equity screening requirements, care management payments, and mandatory downside risk. Extended through June 30, 2030.

name: Home Health Value-Based Purchasing
description: Model tying a portion of home health agency payment to quality performance. Originally piloted in 9 states, expanded nationally in 2022. Agencies can earn up to +5% or face up to -5% payment adjustments based on quality scores. NOTE: this is the ORIGINAL nine-state model, which ended December 31, 2021. The nationwide "expanded HHVBP" operating since 2023 is a separate, permanent program — not this model.

name: Guiding an Improved Dementia Experience
description: CMMI model supporting individuals with dementia and their caregivers. Participants provide interdisciplinary care navigation, 24/7 access, and respite care. Monthly per-beneficiary-per-month payments fund model infrastructure.

name: Value in Opioid Use Disorder Treatment
description: CMMI model testing episode-based payment for opioid use disorder treatment, bundling all services for a 6-month episode. Aims to expand access to evidence-based medication-assisted treatment (MAT). Four-year demonstration scheduled through December 2024.

name: Innovation in Behavioral Health
description: CMMI model integrating physical health services into community behavioral health settings. Practices receive infrastructure and per-member-per-month payments to screen and coordinate care for Medicare and Medicaid beneficiaries.

name: Achieving Healthcare Efficiency through Accountable Design (AHEAD)
description: State-level CMMI model testing all-payer total cost of care approaches. States implement population-based payments spanning Medicare, Medicaid, and commercial payers, with explicit health equity goals. CMS renamed the model in September 2025 from "States Advancing All-Payer Health Equity Approaches"; the AHEAD acronym was retained.

name: Transforming Episode Accountability Model
description: Mandatory episode-based payment model for five surgical procedures: lower extremity joint replacement, surgical hip femur fracture treatment, spinal fusion, coronary artery bypass graft, and major bowel procedure. Hospitals in selected geographic areas are required to participate (721 hospitals, 188 metro areas). 30-day post-discharge episode window — shorter than CJR/BPCI Advanced's 90-day window by design.

name: MA Value-Based Insurance Design Model
description: Tests whether Medicare Advantage plans can use health-condition-specific cost-sharing structures and supplemental benefits to improve care quality and reduce costs. Participating MA plans can offer targeted reduced cost-sharing for high-value services for chronically ill enrollees. CMS ended the model after CY2025, citing excess costs to Medicare.

name: Enhanced Medication Therapy Management
description: CMMI model testing whether enhanced MTM services in Medicare Part D can improve medication adherence and health outcomes for high-risk beneficiaries. Participating Part D plan sponsors were incentivized to increase MTM program participation and reduce hospitalizations.

name: State Innovation Models
description: CMMI initiative providing funding and technical assistance to states developing and testing multi-payer health system transformation models. Two rounds (2013 and 2015) funded 38 states to design and test state-led payment and delivery system reforms across all payers.

name: Financial Alignment Initiative
description: Capitated and managed fee-for-service demonstrations integrating Medicare and Medicaid financing and services for dual-eligible beneficiaries. States partnered with CMS to reduce fragmentation between Medicare and Medicaid for individuals dually enrolled in both programs.

name: PACE Innovation
description: Statutory demonstration expanding PACE (Program of All-Inclusive Care for the Elderly) to new populations and settings. Tests PACE-like models of comprehensive, integrated care for frail elderly individuals who do not yet qualify for nursing home level of care.

name: ACO Long-Term Enhanced Accountable Care Organization Design (LEAD)
description: CMMI model (2027-2036) succeeding ACO REACH, which ends Dec 31, 2026. RFA released March 31, 2026. Fixed 10-year term structured to give ACOs a longer runway for total-cost-of-care accountability than REACH's shorter cycle offered.

name: Comprehensive Care for Joint Replacement Expanded (CJR-X)
description: Mandatory nationwide successor to CJR, which ended December 31, 2024. Extends episode accountability for lower-extremity joint replacement beyond the original 34 metropolitan areas to national scope beginning January 1, 2028.
